title: Existence of a finite ordinary Kähler fourfold program
exact_target: For a normal globally Weil-Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold X with rational klt boundary $\Delta $, does there exist an ordinary negative program starting exactly on X and ending nef for pseudo-effective $K_X+\Delta $, or in a projective relative-Picard-one Mori contraction otherwise, preserving klt and global Weil Q-factoriality and not extracting primes? The composite must not decrease discrepancies and must strictly improve those of contracted X-primes.
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
For a normal globally Weil-Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold X with rational klt boundary $\Delta $, does there exist an ordinary negative program starting exactly on X and ending nef for pseudo-effective $K_X+\Delta $, or in a projective relative-Picard-one Mori contraction otherwise, preserving klt and global Weil Q-factoriality and not extracting primes? The composite must not decrease discrepancies and must strictly improve those of contracted X-primes.

\subsection{Short English statement}
For a normal globally Weil-Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold X with rational klt boundary $\Delta $, does there exist an ordinary negative program starting exactly on X and ending nef for pseudo-effective $K_X+\Delta $, or in a projective relative-Picard-one Mori contraction otherwise, preserving klt and global Weil Q-factoriality and not extracting primes? The composite must not decrease discrepancies and must strictly improve those of contracted X-primes.
